newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-SAMPRAS FEELS AT BACK HOME ON QUEEN'S GRASS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS FEELS AT BACK HOME ON QUEEN'S GRASS.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras strode confidently into the third round of the Queen's grasscourt tournament on Wednesday with a straight sets victory over Argentina's Javier Frana.
The American top seed, looking happy to be back on grass after his third round exit at the French Open, made light work of Frana on an overcast day, advancing 6-3 6-2.
"It was like I never left...I played good out there," said Sampras, winner of the London tournament in 1995.
Sampras, who crashed out to Swede Magnus Norman in Paris while suffering from an upset stomach, was back to his imperious best on the fast grass surface.
The American broke his opponent in the fourth game with a deftly sliced backhand return to move 3-1 ahead.
A lapse of concentration allowed Frana to immediately break back but that seemed to wake up the American and he won the last three games to take the first set.
Frana held serve in the first game of the second set but Sampras then reeled off five games in a row and a subtle drop volley on his second match point at 5-2 was all he needed to secure victory.
"It's always a bit difficult your first grasscourt match after a month-and-a-half on clay but I've got no complaints about the way I played out there," he said.
"I feel fine physically and was pretty solid out there."
Third seed Goran Ivanisevic overcame a slow start to beat India's Leander Paes in straight sets in another second round match.
The 1996 Olympic bronze medallist stretched Ivanisevic to a first set tie-break but the Croat reeled it off 7-1 and took control of the second set to win it 6-3.
Earlier, French Open semifinalist Patrick Rafter dismissed Canada's Sebastien Laureau 6-3 7-5 to move into the round of 16.
The Australian's serve-and-volley game proved to be a surprise success in Roland Garros last week but was predictably successful against the 24-year-old Canadian.
"The French was a great achievement for me and now I just want to keep it going," the ninth seed said.
World number two Michael Chang was due to open his Queen's account against Australia's Scott Draper later on Wednesday.
